title: Which products suit the bracket method?
description: The same bracket method is used for ninety five times eight, one hundred and four times fifteen and forty nine times fifty. A number close to fifty or one hundred is split with a minus or a plus. Keeko doubts the sign for one hundred and four.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number close to a round number is written as the round number minus or plus a small number, and the sign follows the side it lies on. Watch for students who use a minus sign for a number above the round number.

source: Use the same method for 95 × 8, 104 × 15 and 49 × 50, and say which other products suit it.
video_script.why: A learner sees the bracket method on three products and learns which products suit it, with the sign chosen by the side of the round number.
video_script.substitution: Replace the three products with any number close to a round number and any multiplier.
video_script.anchor: three products with a number close to fifty or one hundred, each split into a round number and a small change
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred and four times fifteen is one hundred times fifteen minus four times fifteen
video_script.wrong_move: writes 104 as 100 − 4 although 104 is 4 more than 100, so the sign should be plus
video_script.payoff_line: Ninety five times eight is seven hundred and sixty.

final_answer.spoken: ninety five times eight is seven hundred and sixty, one hundred and four times fifteen is one thousand five hundred and sixty, and forty nine times fifty is two thousand four hundred and fifty

maths_rules: the method suits numbers close to 50, 100 or 1000, such as 99 × 12 and 102 × 25
video_script.design: Three products on a number line, each with its number sitting just before or just after a round number. The sign in the bracket follows the side.

beats.on_screen: To find: the three products, and which other products suit the method

marks.fd1: the two things to find are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find the three products and say which others suit the method.
<bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, ninety five times eight.
Ninety five is five less than one hundred.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>The product is open bracket one hundred minus five close bracket times eight.
Opening the bracket gives one hundred times eight minus five times eight.
<bookmark mark='s13'/>That is eight hundred minus forty.
<bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, one hundred and four times fifteen.
One hundred and four is four more than one hundred.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>The product is open bracket one hundred plus four close bracket times fifteen.
Opening the bracket gives one hundred times fifteen plus four times fifteen.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>That is one thousand five hundred plus sixty.
<bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, forty nine times fifty.
Forty nine is one less than fifty.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>The product is open bracket fifty minus one close bracket times fifty.
Opening the bracket gives fifty times fifty minus one times fifty.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>That is two thousand five hundred minus fifty.

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, look at the numbers we split.
Each was close to fifty or one hundred.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>The method suits a number close to fifty, one hundred or one thousand.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>Ninety nine times twelve and one hundred and two times twenty five suit it.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>Ninety five times eight is seven hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>One hundred and four times fifteen is one thousand five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Forty nine times fifty is two thousand four hundred and fifty.

narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks one hundred and four times fifteen is one hundred times fifteen minus four times fifteen.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But one hundred and four is four more than one hundred, not four less.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>Above one hundred the bracket uses plus.
